questions.q: What is the correct base URI pattern for a Salesforce REST API call?
questions.explain: Every REST call is built on the org's My Domain host plus /services/data/{version}/ as the base path.

questions.q: Which resource would you call to see every API version a given org currently supports?
questions.explain: The unversioned root resource /services/data/ returns a JSON array listing every API version the org currently supports, each with a label and URL.

questions.q: What does the `attributes` object at the top of a REST response record tell you?
options: The record's type and a canonical URL back to it
The access token used to authenticate the request
The SOQL query that produced the record
questions.explain: The attributes object reports {type, url} for the record, which is especially useful when a response could contain records of mixed types.

questions.q: Do you need to send an `attributes` object yourself when creating a new record through the REST API?
options: Yes, every create request must include one
No — attributes only appears in what Salesforce sends back, not in what you send to create or update a record
Only when creating more than one record at a time
Only for custom objects, never for standard objects
questions.explain: attributes is metadata Salesforce adds to responses; create/update request bodies are just flat field:value pairs, with no attributes wrapper needed.

questions.q: Which resource would you use to find out how many API requests an org has remaining in its current daily allocation?
questions.explain: /limits reports the org's remaining allocation across a number of named limits, including DailyApiRequests.
